posts.title: What does a healthy lifestyle really mean?
posts.excerpt: Health isn’t just the absence of illness. Here’s the full picture – and the everyday habits that make the biggest difference.
posts.content:
The World Health Organization defines health as “a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.” In other words: feeling well, coping with everyday life and feeling connected to others all count – not just avoiding the doctor.

The UK picture

Around 64% of adults in England are living with overweight or obesity, and more than a third of adults don’t reach the recommended 150 minutes of activity a week. That raises the risk of long-term conditions and puts extra pressure on the NHS. The good news: small daily changes add up.

The four parts of Total Fitness

  • Physical – heart and lung fitness, muscle strength and flexibility.
  • Mental & emotional – managing stress and keeping a positive outlook.
  • Social – supportive relationships and feeling part of something.
  • Medical – staying free from illness, or safely managing a long-term condition.

Four habits that protect you

  • 🚭 Not smoking – protects your lungs and heart.
  • 🍷 No more than 14 units of alcohol a week, spread over 3 or more days.
  • 🥗 Eating well and staying active – for a healthy weight, strong bones and more energy.
  • 😴 7–9 hours’ sleep and ways to manage stress.

You don’t have to change everything at once. Pick one habit this week and build from there – and if you need support, your GP is a good place to start.

sources.title: NHS England – Health Survey for England
Sport England – Active Lives Adult Survey 2024–25

posts.title: Health is more than not being ill
posts.excerpt: The WHO definition of health covers body, mind and social life. Which one needs your attention this week?
posts.content:
According to the World Health Organization, health is “a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.”

That gives us three areas to look after:

  • 💪 Physical – moving, eating well, sleeping well.
  • 🧠 Mental – coping with stress and looking after your mood.
  • 🤝 Social – time with people who lift you up.

Which one will you focus on this week?

posts.title: The 4 parts of Total Fitness
posts.excerpt: Physical, mental, social and medical – how balanced are yours?
posts.content:
• 💪 Physical – cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength and flexibility.
  • 😌 Mental & emotional – managing stress and keeping a positive mindset.
  • 🤗 Social – supportive relationships and feeling connected.
  • 🩺 Medical – free from illness, or safely managing long-term conditions.

Most of us are stronger in one or two areas than the others. Which one needs a little more attention?

posts.title: 4 habits that protect your health
posts.excerpt: Not smoking, sensible drinking, eating well and good sleep – what each one does for you.
posts.content:
• 🚭 Not smoking – protects your lungs and heart and cuts your risk of cancer and stroke.
  • 🍷 Alcohol: no more than 14 units a week – protects your liver, brain and heart. Check your units.
  • 🥗 Eat well & stay active – a healthy weight, strong bones and muscles, more energy.
  • 😴 7–9 hours’ sleep & less stress – better recovery, focus and resilience.

posts.title: Everyday habits that quietly raise your risk
posts.excerpt: Smoking, too much alcohol, ultra-processed food, sitting all day and poor sleep – and one swap to start with.
posts.content:
🚬 Smoking · 🍺 drinking too much · 🍔 lots of ultra-processed food · 🛋️ long hours of sitting · 🥱 poor sleep.

Over time these can lead to high blood pressure, obesity, heart and circulatory disease, type 2 diabetes, stroke and poorer mental health.

You don’t have to change everything at once – pick one habit to swap out this week.

posts.title: You don’t have to do it alone: your support team
posts.excerpt: GP, dietitian, physiotherapist, counsellor – who does what, and where to find trusted information.
posts.content:
• 🩺 GP – your first stop for any health worry, and the route to most NHS services.
  • 🥗 Registered Dietitian – evidence-based advice on food and nutrition.
  • 🏋️ Physiotherapist – help with injuries, pain and moving safely.
  • 💬 Mental health counsellor – talking therapies. In England you can refer yourself to NHS Talking Therapies.

For trusted information, use nhs.uk and NHS Better Health.

posts.title: Is your plate actually balanced? The Eatwell Guide explained
posts.excerpt: The UK’s official healthy-eating model in plain English – food groups, easy swaps, nutrients and hydration.
posts.content:
The Eatwell Guide is the UK’s official picture of a healthy, balanced diet. It isn’t about one meal – it shows the balance to aim for across a day or a week.

Build a balanced plate

  1. Fruit & vegetables – just over a third of what you eat. Aim for at least 5 portions a day.
  2. Starchy carbohydrates – another third. Choose wholegrain or higher-fibre versions.
  3. Beans, pulses, fish, eggs, meat & other proteins – aim for 2 portions of fish a week, one of them oily.
  4. Dairy & alternatives – choose lower-fat and lower-sugar options.
  5. Oils & spreads – unsaturated, and in small amounts.

Simple swaps

Sugary drinks → water. White bread → wholemeal. Crisps → unsalted nuts or fruit. Fried → grilled, steamed or baked.

Watch the salt, sugar & saturated fat

Too much raises the risk of obesity, type 2 diabetes, heart disease, high blood pressure and tooth decay. Check front-of-pack labels – more greens, fewer reds.

Don’t forget drinks

Aim for 6 to 8 cups or glasses of fluid a day. Water, lower-fat milk and sugar-free drinks, including tea and coffee, all count.

Need tailored advice? Speak to your GP or a Registered Dietitian.

sources.title: NHS – Water, drinks and your health

posts.title: Eat the rainbow: your 5 A Day
posts.excerpt: At least 5 portions of fruit and veg a day – and fresh, frozen, tinned or dried all count.
posts.content:
Aim for at least 5 portions of a variety of fruit and vegetables every day 🍎🥦🥕🍌🍅

Fresh, frozen, tinned and dried all count. One adult portion is 80g – roughly a handful. 30g of dried fruit counts as a portion, and so does one 150ml glass of fruit juice or smoothie a day (but only one).

Try our 5 A Day counter to see how you’re doing today.

posts.title: Your plate, balanced

1. Fruit & vegetables
  2. Starchy carbohydrates (choose high-fibre)

posts.content:
• 🥤 Sugary drinks → 💧 water or sugar-free drinks
  • 🥖 White bread / pasta → 🍞 wholemeal
  • 🍫 Crisps / chocolate → 🥜 unsalted nuts or fresh fruit

posts.title: Fibre first
posts.excerpt: Base your meals on high-fibre starchy carbohydrates – here’s what to pick.
posts.content:
Base your meals on high-fibre starchy carbohydrates:

  • 🍞 Wholemeal bread
  • 🍚 Brown rice
  • 🥣 Oats
  • 🥔 Potatoes with their skins on

Fibre supports healthy digestion and helps you feel full. Adults should aim for 30g of fibre a day – most of us get less than that.

posts.title: Stay hydrated: 6 to 8 glasses a day
posts.excerpt: How much to drink, what counts, and why it matters.
posts.content:
Aim for 6 to 8 cups or glasses of fluid a day. Water, lower-fat milk and sugar-free drinks, including tea and coffee, all count. You may need more when it’s hot or when you’re active.

Good hydration helps regulate body temperature, supports focus and digestion, and helps prevent headaches and tiredness.

posts.title: Watch the salt, sugar & saturated fat
posts.excerpt: What too much can do, and how food labels help.
posts.content:
Too much salt, sugar and saturated fat increases the risk of obesity, type 2 diabetes, heart disease, high blood pressure and tooth decay.

Check food labels and choose lower-salt, lower-sugar options where you can. Need tailored advice? See a Registered Dietitian or your GP.

posts.title: How much should you really move?
posts.excerpt: The UK Chief Medical Officers’ guidelines for adults, explained – plus the benefits, the 3 types of activity, and when to pause.
posts.content:
The guidelines (adults 19–64)

  • ⏱️ 150 minutes of moderate activity a week – brisk walking, cycling, swimming – or 75 minutes of vigorous activity like running or sport, or a mix of both.
  • 💪 Strength activities on at least 2 days a week, working all the major muscle groups.
  • 🪑 Break up long periods of sitting.

Short bouts of any length count, and you can spread the minutes over the week in whatever way suits you. If you’re starting from nothing, any activity is better than none.

What it protects you from

Regular activity lowers your risk of coronary heart disease, type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, stroke, osteoporosis and some cancers.

Mix all 3 types

🚣 Aerobic for heart and lungs · 🧗 Strength for muscles and bones · 🤸 Flexibility & balance for joints and stability.

Know when to pause

Put exercise on hold if you have a fever or viral infection, chest pain, dizziness, an acute injury or uncontrolled high blood pressure. Pregnant or managing a long-term condition? Talk to your GP, a physiotherapist or an exercise referral specialist first.

Track your week with our activity tracker.

posts.title: Health vs fitness – what’s the difference?
posts.excerpt: Regular moderate movement for health; structured training for fitness. Both matter.
posts.content:
🚶 General health comes from regular, moderate daily movement.

🏋️ Physical fitness comes from structured, higher-intensity training that gradually gets harder (progressive overload).

Both matter – start where you are.

posts.content:
Put exercise on hold if you have:

  • 🤒 A fever or viral infection
  • 💔 Chest pain

posts.title: Movement is medicine
posts.excerpt: What being active does inside your body – for your heart, blood sugar, mind, bones, back and lungs.
posts.content:
Regular physical activity can lower your risk of major illnesses like coronary heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes and some cancers – and lower your risk of early death by up to 30%.

❤️ Heart

More than 8 million people in the UK live with heart and circulatory disease. Activity helps lower blood pressure, improves cholesterol and keeps your heart muscle strong.

🩸 Blood sugar

Working muscles use glucose for fuel, and regular activity helps your body use insulin better – lowering your risk of type 2 diabetes.

🧠 Mind

Each year, 1 in 4 people in England experience a mental health problem. Moving more can lift your mood, ease stress and help you sleep.

🦴 Bones & joints

Over 50, 1 in 2 women and 1 in 5 men will break a bone because of osteoporosis. Weight-bearing and strength activity help keep bones strong.

🧘 Back

With most back pain, staying active helps you recover faster than resting in bed.

🫁 Lungs

Living with asthma? Warm up gradually, carry your reliever inhaler and use your preventer as prescribed.

Living with a health condition?

Check with your GP or nurse first, start low and go slow, and stop and get help if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.

sources.title: Mind – Mental health facts and statistics
Asthma + Lung UK – Exercise and asthma

posts.title: 8 million+: protect your heart
posts.excerpt: More than 8 million people in the UK live with heart and circulatory disease.
posts.content:
More than 8 million people in the UK are living with heart and circulatory disease.

Regular activity is one of the best things you can do for your heart: it helps lower blood pressure, improves cholesterol and keeps your heart muscle strong.

Start where you are – a brisk 10-minute walk counts 🚶

posts.title: Build bones that last
posts.excerpt: 1 in 2 women and 1 in 5 men over 50 will break a bone because of osteoporosis.
posts.content:
Over the age of 50, 1 in 2 women and 1 in 5 men will break a bone because of osteoporosis.

Weight-bearing and strength activities help keep your bones strong: brisk walking, dancing, stair climbing and strength training.

It’s never too early – or too late – to start.

posts.title: Your heart on exercise
posts.excerpt: Blood pressure down, “good” cholesterol up – what activity does for your heart.
posts.content:
• ⬇️ Blood pressure goes down
  • ⬆️ “Good” HDL cholesterol goes up
  • 💪 Your heart muscle gets stronger
  • 〰️ Your blood vessels stay more flexible

All of this adds up to a lower risk of heart disease and stroke.

posts.title: 1 in 4: move for your mind
posts.excerpt: Each year 1 in 4 people in England experience a mental health problem. Movement can help.
posts.content:
Each year, 1 in 4 people in England experience a mental health problem.

Moving your body can help you lift your mood, ease stress and anxiety, sleep better and connect with others.

If you’re struggling, you don’t have to cope alone – talk to your GP or someone you trust. In a crisis, call NHS 111 (option 2) or Samaritans on 116 123.

sources.title: Mind – Mental health facts and statistics

posts.title: Back pain? Keep moving.
posts.excerpt: What to do – and avoid – with most everyday back pain.
posts.content:
✅ Do carry on with daily activities as much as you can, and try walking, swimming, yoga or pilates.

❌ Avoid long periods in bed, and sitting still for hours without a break.

See a GP if the pain doesn’t improve within a few weeks or keeps getting worse.

posts.title: Living with a health condition? Stay active, safely
posts.excerpt: Check first, start low, go slow – and know the warning signs.
posts.content:
• 🩺 Check with your GP or nurse first
  • 🐢 Start low, go slow
  • 🔥 Warm up and cool down
  • 💊 Keep your medication handy (for example an inhaler or glucose tablets)

Stop and get help if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.

posts.title: What’s stopping you? 6 barriers and how to beat them
posts.excerpt: No time, no money, too old, the kids, boredom or nerves – a realistic fix for each.
posts.content:
Around 1 in 4 adults in England do less than 30 minutes of physical activity a week – and in London, about a third of adults aren’t meeting the recommended levels. Most of us have a reason. Here are the six we hear most, and a fix for each.

⏳ “I don’t have time.”

Every minute counts. Activity of any length adds up towards your 150 minutes – take the stairs, walk part of your commute, get out at lunchtime.

💷 “I can’t afford a gym.”

Move for free. Brisk walks, the free NHS Couch to 5K app, parkrun, home workouts and your local park cost nothing.

👵 “I’m too old to start.”

It’s never too late. Start gently and build up. Over 65? Add strength and balance activities on 2 days a week.

🧒 “I’ve got the kids with me.”

Make it family time. Walk or scoot to school, play in the park, have a kitchen disco – kids copy what they see.

🥱 “I just don’t enjoy exercise.”

Find your thing. It doesn’t have to be the gym – dance, garden, cycle, swim or walk with a friend.

😰 “I feel nervous and out of place.”

Start small, bring a buddy. Step a little outside your comfort zone at a time. Health worries? Ask your GP.

Your move: pick one barrier and try one fix this week.

posts.title: 11.8 million adults do less than 30 minutes a week
posts.excerpt: About 1 in 4 adults in England are inactive. Going from nothing to a little makes the biggest difference.
posts.content:
That’s how many adults in England do less than 30 minutes of physical activity a week – roughly 1 in 4 of us.

The good news: the biggest health gains come from going from nothing to even a little. If you’re starting from zero, a short walk today really does count.

posts.title: 150 minutes a week is about 21 minutes a day
posts.excerpt: Short bouts count – or fit it into one or two longer sessions.
posts.content:
That’s the UK goal for moderate activity. Short bouts of any length count, or you can fit it into 1 or 2 longer sessions if that suits your week better.

Add strength activities on at least 2 days a week too 💪

posts.title: Free ways to move in London
posts.excerpt: No gym? No problem. Walks, Couch to 5K, parkrun, home workouts and active travel.
posts.content:
• 🚶 Brisk walking – London’s parks, canals and the Thames Path are on your doorstep.
  • 📱 NHS Couch to 5K app – a free plan from the couch to 5K in 9 weeks.
  • 🏃 parkrun – free weekly 5K events: walk, jog or run.
  • 🏠 Home workouts – bodyweight moves, no kit needed.
  • 🚲 Active travel – walk or cycle short trips.

posts.title: Myth vs fact: exercise edition
posts.excerpt: Does it only count at the gym? Are short bursts pointless? Is it too late?
posts.content:
❌ It only counts if you’re sweating at the gym.
✅ Brisk walking, gardening, dancing and cycling all count.

❌ Short bursts are pointless.
✅ Activity of any length adds up and benefits your health.

❌ I’ve left it too late.
✅ It’s never too late – start gently and build up.

posts.title: Small wins, big confidence
posts.excerpt: The best way to build belief in yourself is with small, repeatable wins.
posts.content:
Believing you can do something is a big part of actually doing it – and the best way to build that belief is with small wins.

  1. Pick something you know you can do
  2. Do it 3 times this week
  3. Notice it feels easier
  4. Add a little more

Feeling nervous? Bring a friend along – it’s easier together 🤝

posts.excerpt: Motivation that lasts comes from within. Finish the sentence: “I want to move more so I can…”
posts.content:
Motivation that lasts comes from within – knowing what moving more means to you.

Finish the sentence: “I want to move more so I can…”

  • 🧒 keep up with my kids
  • 😴 sleep better
  • 😌 feel less stressed
  • 🏡 stay independent
  • 💪 feel proud of myself
